svg.title: Figure 5. Column curve for 6061-T6
svg.desc: Critical stress against effective slenderness ratio for 6061-T6 aluminum, from 0 to 350. Euler's hyperbola rises without limit as the slenderness falls and crosses the yield strength (a horizontal line at about 274 MPa) near L_e/r = 50; the region to the left is shaded because there Euler predicts a stress the material cannot carry. The tangent-modulus curve, from Lab 1's stress-strain curve, leaves Euler's hyperbola below about L_e/r = 60 and stays under the yield strength until very short columns; the reduced-modulus curve lies slightly above it. The Aluminum Association allowable-stress curve (with its factor of safety) runs well below both. Tick marks along the bottom show the slenderness of this lab's tests: Part D at about 49, the 300 mm pinned bar and the ideal fixed-fixed 600 mm bar at about 164, the ideal fixed-pinned 640 mm bar near 244, the 450 mm bar of Parts A and C at about 245, and the 600 mm pinned bar at about 327.
